From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Clearline model-fit recap, recommended trials & acceptance gates

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the POC: 

Summary of demo/notes
- Primary workload: account verification + customer message routing + simple balance-explanation NLU (short responses, strict correctness high priority)
- Current in-house baseline: “Clearline Core” (rule-weighted ensemble + smaller proprietary encoder) — you noted latency target ~250ms p50 and high precision on entity extraction.

Redwood recommendations (trial plan)
1) Models to trial (two simultaneous arms):
   - Open candidate: o3-large-v2 (8B, float16), with our suggested prompt wrapper and safety filters.
   - Redwood-optimized compact: rwd-compat-3.5-q4 (6B quantized) — higher throughput with KV caching for conversation state.

2) Acceptance gates (preliminary — we can tighten after initial week):
   - Entity extraction F1 >= 0.86 on the provided labeled sample set (we'll share prompt-set and eval harness).
   - Response precision (contractual responses like balance or account status) >= 98% exact-match on validation prompts.
   - Latency p50 <= 300ms, p95 <= 750ms under the trial traffic profile (we'll supply recommended load generator).

3) Quality/regression concerns vs Clearline Core
   - Edge-case hallucination on rare account codes; propose an explicit fallback policy (verified facts only) and a soft-block for out-of-scope answers.
   - We’ll run a “diff” eval against your samples to highlight where open models deviate from Clearline Core; that will let us set targeted prompt constraints or a small verification wrapper.

Attachments I’m including: prompt_sets_clearline_v1.json (sample prompts & expected outputs), bench_preview_clearline.csv (initial microbenchmarks), trial_playbook.pdf (trial runbook + roles/responsibilities).

Proposed timeline & next steps
- Week 0 (this week): share credentials and enable sandbox traffic; kick off two-arm trial for 14 calendar days.
- Week 1: midpoint review (metric digest + three example regressions flagged).
- Week 2: decision readout and recommendation (open model vs rwd-compat vs hybrid fallback).

Ask: Can you confirm procurement / legal lead so we can ship the trial paperwork? Also confirm whether you prefer the hosted sandbox (fastest) or a dedicated VPC trial (if you need isolation).

Estimate: based on your described traffic, we estimate ~1.2M tokens for a 2-week discovery run (hosted). We’ll convert that to a proposed trial credit line in the order form.

I’ll loop Priyom on scoping and Marissa for the eval harness — we’ll be deliberate about the regression threshold so the decision is data-driven.

Best,
Hannah

- Procurement/legal: I’ve copied our procurement lead (procurement@clearline.com) to start the paperwork. We’ll need a short form NDA + trial order form — can Redwood provide a stamped SOW?

Quick internal notes / action items before sandbox kickoff: 

- Ownership: Priyom -> trial orchestration (credentials, endpoint lifecycle), Marissa -> eval harness + labeled sample ingest. Hannah -> exec sponsor / procurement touchpoint.
- Answer to Sara q1: quantized rwd-compat-3.5-q4 has a small delta in some fine-grained NER cases vs o3-large-v2. Mitigations: prompt engineering (+ constrained decoding on entity spans) and post-hoc verifier (small bert-ish classifier for entity sanity checks). We should call this out explicitly in the trial playbook.
- Answer to Sara q2: yes, the verification/fallback can be toggled at the routing layer without a model redeploy (we’ll provide a toggle in the sandbox route config).

I’ll prepare a short tech-readout doc that lays out: expected metric deltas, config knobs (batching, kv-cache TTLs, verification toggle), and a minimal runner to produce the midpoint digest. Planning to send that Friday EOD.
